children: Coinbase Chief Executive Officer Brian Armstrong said Bitcoin has likely already passed the bottom of the current downturn. If it regains upward momentum starting next year, he said, the token could climb above $400,000 by 2030. That would be more than six times its recent price of about $60,000.

Speaking at the TomorrowX event in Austin, Texas, Armstrong said it appears this cycle has already hit its low. He added that this cycle’s bottom was about four times the trough of the previous cycle and projected Bitcoin could top $400,000 by 2030.

He said Bitcoin’s recent weakness was partly driven by capital moving ahead of the planned initial public offering of artificial intelligence company Anthropic. Armstrong added that a similar shift took place before SpaceX’s listing, when funds moved from Bitcoin into stocks and returned a few months later, suggesting the current selling pressure could also be temporary.

Coinbase, meanwhile, is expanding into stocks, derivatives and prediction markets as it seeks to reduce its reliance on revenue from spot crypto trading. Armstrong said new products such as prediction markets and derivatives now account for about 25% of Coinbase’s trading-fee revenue. Coinbase said in its third-quarter earnings report that prediction-market revenue alone had surpassed $200 million on an annualized basis.

Armstrong said trading volume through AI agents has recently been increasing by about 20% from a week earlier. Coinbase is developing dedicated accounts and payment systems that would allow users to delegate portfolio rebalancing and order execution to AI. He added that the company is also building features that would let users set spending limits and require direct approval for trades above a certain size.

title: Coinbase CEO Armstrong Says Bitcoin Likely Bottomed, Could Exceed $400,000 by 2030
